trust_decision.summary: Whether a configuration or command-line value may be returned verbatim to an unauthenticated API client is decided by key-name matching only: Config.as_dict_secure() redacts a value when the option NAME matches _SECURE_SENSITIVE_KEY_RE, and GlancesRestfulApi._sanitize_args() redacts a hardcoded key list, so any credential carried inside the VALUE (a URL userinfo such as https://user:pass@host) is returned in full, and a login stored under a key the pattern does not spell out (e.g. public_username, influxdb user) is returned in full.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names as_dict_secure() and /api/4/config by name, so an engineer greps the method and lands on the one-line dict comprehension that decides 'vulnerable' purely by option key name, never looking at the value.

fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP API output module (separate, hand-maintained redaction implementation in the outputs package)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: GET /api/4/args has no reachable leak today (no argument carries a URL userinfo, and -u <login> forces a password at glances/main.py:812, so the unauthenticated args view cannot hold a real login), and the [ports] web_N_url is a monitored target rather than a configured secret — each looks like a neighbouring feature rather than part of the same value-level rule.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate non-credential values sit right next to the sink and must survive: the CPU/load/per-CPU thresholds whose option names start with 'user' (user_careful, user_warning, user_critical, user_log) must stay visible or the Web UI loses its threshold display, and non-string values (bools/ints/floats: password_prompt, port, time) must keep their JSON type in /api/4/args rather than becoming '********' or a string.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: glances/config.py:248 (set_default_cwc('percpu','user')); conf/glances.conf:176,207 (user_careful=50) consumed as limits at glances/plugins/plugin/model.py:739-745; arg types at glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py:1369-1378

O6_input_shapes: sensitive key with a plain string value (public_password, public_username)
non-string value: bool/int/float returned unchanged (password_prompt, port, time)
URL value carrying userinfo, e.g. https://admin:secret123@ipv4.ipleak.net/json/ -> https://********@host/...
URL value without userinfo left untouched (host, public_field)
several distinct credential-bearing URL keys in different sections (web_1_url, web_2_url); the fix's sub() also covers several occurrences inside one value
key that merely starts with 'user' but is not a login (user_careful / user_critical / user_log) must NOT be redacted
whole blocked section ([passwords]) still omitted rather than per-value redacted

O7_producer.where: glances/web_list.py:51-65 copies the [ports] web_N_url value verbatim into a plugin stats dict (and derives description from urlparse(url).netloc, which itself contains the userinfo when description is unset), so the same credential exists in a second structure the check never inspects; the config-file side is loaded by Config.read at glances/config.py:182-190

O8_uncovered_routes.where: glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py:1002 (get_api) and :949 (getAllAsDict) with the producer at glances/web_list.py:51-65 and glances/plugins/ports/__init__.py:83-86
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The value is a target URL the ports plugin scans (glances/plugins/ports/__init__.py:309), not a credential the user configured for Glances; it is served as plugin stats, not from the /api/4/config endpoint the advisory names, and redacting it at the producer would break monitoring.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package file glances/web_list.py plus glances/plugins/ports/__init__.py, collected by the handler in glances/outputs/glances_restful_api.py — 2 packages, 3 files from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.distance: glances/outputs/glances_mcp.py, a third module in the outputs package, one plugin-stats hop from glances/plugins/ports/__init__.py:83-86 — 2 packages, 3 files

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second URL-list loader (a new [webhook]/[amp] style section, or a ports_list variant) that copies a config value verbatim into JSON-served plugin stats
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: web_list.py already does exactly this for [ports] and even synthesises description from urlparse(url).netloc, so a maintainer adding another monitored-URL list would copy the same pattern and inherit the same leak.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Exposing the browser-mode server entry (server['uri'], built as http://username:password@host:port) or a new 'url' field through /api/4/serverslist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_uri() already composes a credential-bearing URL and stores it in the server dict at :166, and the servers list is already served unauthenticated; only the key-name pop in _sanitize_server keeps it hidden.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A value-level check inside _sanitize_server, which pops 'password' and 'uri' by key name but leaves any other field (e.g. username, alias) in plaintext
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a third hand-maintained redaction list in the same file as _sanitize_args; a maintainer who learned the key-list lesson once would plausibly extend it here, or new server fields would slip past it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A route or export that serves Config.items(section) (already used by glances/password_list.py:38 and glances/plugins/plugin/model.py:739) instead of as_dict_secure()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: items() is the raw accessor sitting one line below as_dict_secure(); any new endpoint or export that wants 'just one section' would reach for it and bypass the sanitiser entirely.

O9_family: exposure of sensitive information / credential disclosure to unauthenticated clients (CWE-200; key-name-only redaction bypassed at value level)

O10_build.toolchain: pyproject.toml + setuptools/uv (Makefile: uv run pytest, pytest). Web API needs the [web] extra (fastapi, uvicorn, python-jose, requests); MCP needs the [mcp] extra (mcp>=1.0.0).
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_restful.py:281 test_014_config starts a live server on localhost:61234 and only asserts that /api/4/config is a dict (no redaction assertion); tests/test_api.py exercises GlancesAPI in-process; tests/test_plugin_ports.py covers only the ports alert levels. No test at the pinned commit touches as_dict_secure() or _sanitize_args() — the fix's tests/test_api_secure.py does not exist here.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Widen the key-name regex in glances/config.py (add username|user|login) and add the URL regex inside as_dict_secure only, leaving _sanitize_args and every plugin-stats export (REST /api/4/ports, MCP, XML-RPC) untouched — or, on the other side, redact at the producer glances/web_list.py:51 so the ports scanner can no longer reach the URL it must HEAD.
